subject: Model shortlist & token provisioning for BlueNexus onboarding
messages:
From: Rita Halvorsen <rita@bluenexus.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@bluenexus.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: onboarding questions — model shortlist + token cadence

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — BlueNexus is excited to move into the pilot. Before we schedule the implementation kickoff we need a concrete model shortlist and an initial token provisioning estimate for our payments reconciliation use case.

High-level details:
- Expected avg prompt length: ~250 tokens (multi-field JSON payload)
- Expected reply length: ~120 tokens (concise classification + short explanation)
- Peak concurrency: ~40 QPS during settlement windows (approx. 10 mins, 2x/day)
- Monthly active volume: estimate TBD but planning a 3-month pilot with roughly 2M requests/month as an upper bound

Can you provide: 1) 2–3 recommended model variants (including quantized options) with latency/cost tradeoffs, 2) an initial token/month estimate and suggested committed capacity for Redwood Dedicated or Hosted (we're evaluating both), and 3) any immediate configuration limits (context length, token caps) we should plan for?

Also please include any artifacts we can attach to our procurement packet.

Best,
Rita
Rita Halvorsen
Head of Platform Operations | BlueNexus
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Rita Halvorsen <rita@bluenexus.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: onboarding questions — model shortlist + token cadence

Hi Rita — great to meet you on the demo call. Attaching a compact spreadsheet with our initial token math for the pilot (bluenexus_token_estimates_v1.xlsx). Summary below so you can paste into procurement: 

Proposed model shortlist (tiered by latency vs cost):
1) Redwood-RT-3B-q4 (quantized) — best cost per token, expected median gen latency ~45–70ms on Dedicated 1xA10 instance, recommended for bulk reconciliation tasks where speed is secondary.
2) L2-7B-q4f8 — balanced latency/cost, median ~30–50ms, good for mixed workloads and provides higher quality on nuanced explanations.
3) Redwood-Large-13B (fp16) — highest quality, median ~80–120ms, use as fallback for complex exceptions.

Context length guidance: all three support up to 8k tokens; our suggested operational context cap for the pilot is 4k tokens (prompt + history + system) to keep latency predictable. If you need longer context for dispute histories, we can enable 8k during a phased test.

Token estimate (pilot month, conservative):
- Avg tokens/request = prompt 250 + response 120 = 370 tokens
- Requests/month = 2,000,000 -> tokens/month = 740,000,000 tokens (~740M)
- If you choose a tiered split (80% on Redwood-RT-3B-q4, 15% on L2-7B-q4f8, 5% on 13B fallback) we can provide weighted latency and cost estimates in the spreadsheet.

Recommended committed capacity: for predictable peaks, reserve Dedicated slots to cover 50 QPS sustained during windowing plus autoscale for bursts. If you prefer Hosted, we recommend a committed unit with burst credits for settlement windows.

I've cc'd Monica and Ben — Monica will share the implementation checklist and a short mutual action plan. Let me know if you'd rather we map this into a one-page summary for procurement.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Sr. Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachment: bluenexus_token_estimates_v1.xlsx
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rita Halvorsen <rita@bluenexus.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Sep 2025 10:32:00 -0700
Subject: RE: onboarding questions — model shortlist + token cadence

Thanks Michael — adding a short implementation breakdown and next steps. Attaching implementation_checklist_v2.pdf. Key points and asks from CS/Implementation perspective:

1) Confirmation items for BlueNexus (reply please):
   - Pilot requests/month: confirm expected range (we used 0.5M / 1M / 2M in spreadsheet bins)
   - Percent of requests requiring full 4k context vs single-shot prompts
   - Any PII/data residency constraints (we'll map to Private deployment if required)

2) Model routing suggestion (we propose a simple policy for pilot):
   - Default route -> Redwood-RT-3B-q4
   - If explanation_length > 250 chars or rule-match confidence < 0.7 -> route to L2-7B-q4f8
   - Exception handling -> Redwood-Large-13B (fp16) fallback with sampling rate 5% for monitoring

3) Operational knobs we'll configure for you:
   - Prefix cache for static request headers to reduce tokens
   - KV cache TTL for short-lived conversation state during settlement windows (10m)
   - Autoscale policy: baseline 50 QPS, pod burst to 120 QPS for 5 min window (safely handles 2x-day spikes)

4) Timeline (we suggest):
   - Thu 9/18: Procurement packet + SOW sent (we'll provide one-pager)
   - Mon 9/22: Implementation kickoff (engineering + CS)
   - Week of 9/29: Pilot smoke tests and latency baseline measurement

Please confirm the requested bins and whether procurement wants a Hosted vs Dedicated cost comparison. If procurement needs a short one-page cost appendix, we can turn the spreadsheet into that asset.

Thanks — looking forward to kickoff.
Monica Patel
Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference
Attachments: implementation_checklist_v2.pdf, model_shortlist_notes.md
From: Rita Halvorsen <rita@bluenexus.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: onboarding questions — model shortlist + token cadence

Perfect, this is exactly what procurement needed.

We confirm the pilot target at the 1M requests/month bin for month 1 (scaling to 2M if smoke tests look good). Roughly 20% of requests will need the full 4k context (dispute chains), the rest are single-shot. No cross-border data residency issues for the pilot.

We'll proceed with the Hosted comparison for cost appendix; procurement (procurement@bluenexus.ai) will review the spreadsheet and expects a one-page appendix by 9/18. Please send the SOW and procurement packet to that inbox.

I'll also approve Monday 9/22 for the kickoff — invite engineering and the support contacts. I'll route DocuSign to our buyer after we get the appendix.

Thanks everyone — excited to get started.
Rita
Head of Platform Operations | BlueNexus
